tagline: Istanbul's most expat-friendly neighbourhood — bohemian, hilly, and full of the city's best brunch spots.

items.name: Cihangir Café
items.description: The neighbourhood's most iconic café. Mismatched furniture, good espresso, and a crowd of locals and expats who've been coming for years.
items.tip: Go on a weekday morning for the best atmosphere. Saturdays get packed.

items.name: Coffee Manifesto
items.description: One of the best specialty coffee roasters in Istanbul. Clean, minimalist space with excellent single-origin filter coffee.

items.name: Smyrna Café & Brunch
items.description: An Aegean-inspired café with a great brunch menu and a quiet terrace overlooking Cihangir Park.
items.tip: Their menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs) is outstanding.

items.name: Jash
items.description: The best brunch spot in Cihangir — possibly the city. Armenian-inspired menu, fresh ingredients, long communal tables.
items.tip: Queue starts at 10am on weekends. They don't take reservations — arrive early or be prepared to wait.

items.name: Datli Maya
items.description: A beloved bakery and organic café run by a Turkish-American couple. Incredible sourdough, pastries, and healthy lunch options.

items.name: Zübeyir Ocakbaşı
items.description: Legendary charcoal grill restaurant. The Adana kebap and lamb chops are among the best in Istanbul. Lively, atmospheric setting.
items.tip: Dinner only. Book ahead on weekends — it fills up fast.

items.name: Karaköy Lokantası
items.description: Modern Turkish cuisine at its best. Fresh, seasonal menus and a calm atmosphere. Perfect for a proper sit-down lunch.

items.name: Leb-i Derya Richmond
items.description: Rooftop bar with some of the best views of the Bosphorus in the city. Great cocktails and a crowd that knows how to enjoy them.
items.tip: Book ahead for the terrace on weekends. The view at dusk is spectacular.

items.name: Hayal Kahvesi Cihangir
items.description: A Cihangir institution. Intimate bar with live music most nights — jazz, blues, Turkish rock. Very local crowd.

items.name: Peyote
items.description: Small, eclectic bar with a strong alternative music programme. Good craft beers, friendly staff, neighbourhood feel.

items.name: Cihangir Park
items.description: The neighbourhood's living room. A small hilltop park where locals sit, chat, and watch the Bosphorus. Perfect in the evening.

items.name: Vintage & Antique Shops
items.description: Cihangir is packed with small antique and vintage shops along Faik Paşa Yokuşu and Akarsu Yokuşu. Budget a few hours.
items.tip: Prices are negotiable if you're polite about it. Go on weekday afternoons when it's quieter.

items.name: Walk to Galata Tower
items.description: A 10-minute downhill walk through atmospheric streets takes you to Galata Tower and Karaköy. One of the best urban walks in Istanbul.

tips: Cihangir is hilly — comfortable shoes are essential. Many of the best spots are on steep side streets.
Many Smileys members live here, making it a great neighbourhood for spontaneous meet-ups.
The 10-minute walk downhill to Karaköy is one of the best in Istanbul — take it over a taxi.
Most cafés have wi-fi and tolerate working from them for hours. It's that kind of neighbourhood.
